name: dig
description: A flexible DNS lookup utility: queries specific record types, specific servers, and shows full response details.

flags.description: Query a specific DNS server, e.g. @8.8.8.8 or @1.1.1.1.
Record type: A, AAAA, MX, TXT, NS, CNAME, ANY.
Follow delegation from the root servers down — shows how resolution really works.

examples.explanation: Just the A record — the fastest way to resolve a name in scripts.
Mail servers for the domain, with priority.
Queries Google DNS directly, bypassing your system resolver — the standard test for "is my DNS server lying?".
Reverse DNS: resolves an IP back to its hostname.
Reads TXT records — where SPF, DKIM, and domain-verification tokens live.

about: dig shows the full DNS conversation: QUESTION, ANSWER, AUTHORITY, and the query time plus server that answered. The flags line reveals DNSSEC status (do flag) and recursion. nslookup and host are simpler front ends; dig gives the complete picture.
mistakes: Reading the default "ANSWER: 0" as an error — it means the name has no record of the requested type.
Forgetting +short in scripts and parsing decorated output.
